events.title: American Gas Association, et al. v. Dept. of Energy, et al.: Certiorari Granted and Case Remanded
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted the petition for a writ of certiorari in the case of American Gas Association, et al. v. Dept. of Energy, et al., vacated the judgment, and remanded the case to the United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit. The remand was for further consideration in light of the position asserted by the Solicitor General in a brief filed on April 28, 2026.
events.why_relevant: This action underscores the influence of the Solicitor General's position on the Court's decision to remand cases for further review.

events.title: Olivarria, Louis v. California: Certiorari Granted and Case Remanded
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted the motion for leave to proceed in forma pauperis and the petition for a writ of certiorari in the case of Olivarria, Louis v. California. The judgment was vacated, and the case was remanded to the Court of Appeal of California, Third Appellate District, for further consideration in light of the position asserted by California in its brief filed on May 6, 2026.
events.why_relevant: This decision highlights the Court's role in ensuring state appellate decisions are revisited in light of new arguments or evidence.

events.title: Texas v. New Mexico, et al.: United States’ Claims Dismissed
events.summary: The Supreme Court dismissed with prejudice the United States' claims in the original jurisdiction case of Texas v. New Mexico, et al. This dismissal concludes the federal government's involvement in the dispute between the states.
events.why_relevant: The dismissal of federal claims in interstate disputes reflects the Court's management of its original jurisdiction docket.

events.title: United States v. Johnson, Shaheem: Certiorari Granted and Case Remanded
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted the petition for a writ of certiorari in the case of United States v. Johnson, Shaheem, vacated the judgment, and remanded the case to the United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit. This decision was made for further consideration in light of the recent rulings in Fernandez v. United States and Rutherford v. United States. Justices Sotomayor and Jackson dissented, indicating they would have denied the petition.
events.why_relevant: This decision reflects the Supreme Court's role in ensuring lower court decisions align with recent precedents.

events.title: Walters, Dir., VA DOC v. Coleman, Christopher: Certiorari Granted and Case Remanded
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted the motion for leave to proceed in forma pauperis and the petition for a writ of certiorari in the case of Walters, Dir., VA DOC v. Coleman, Christopher. The judgment was vacated, and the case was remanded to the United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit for further consideration in light of Clark v. Sweeney.
events.why_relevant: This order demonstrates the Court's oversight in ensuring that appellate decisions are reconsidered in light of relevant legal standards.

events.title: Supreme Court denies stay in Lovelace v. Lee
events.summary: The Supreme Court of the United States denied the application for a stay or vacatur in the case of Lovelace, Commissioner, Alabama Department of Corrections, et al. v. Jeffery Lee. The application was initially presented to Justice Thomas, who referred it to the full Court. Justices Thomas, Alito, and Gorsuch indicated they would have granted the application, but the majority did not agree, resulting in the denial of the stay or vacatur.
events.why_relevant: The denial of a stay or vacatur affects the immediate legal proceedings and enforcement of lower court decisions in this case.
